title: Review of the Case of Parti Liyani v Public Prosecutor 2020 SGHC 187
what_it_is: Review of the Case of Parti Liyani v Public Prosecutor 2020 SGHC 187

sections.label: High Court acquittal on appeal
sections.summary: She appealed to the High Court against her conviction and sentence, and was acquitted on all charges on 4 September 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Minister for Home Affairs and Law Mr Shanmugam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: She appealed to the High Court against her conviction and sentence, and on 4 September 2020, she was acquitted on all the charges by the High Court.

sections.label: Broader questions about case
sections.summary: News reports and commentaries raised broader questions about whether LML worked the system, whether Police and AGC unfairly prosecuted Ms Liyani, whether she got a fair trial, and whether there is one law for the wealthy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Many news reports and commentaries on this, since September.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There has been interest because underlying these questions, which are specific to the case, there is a broader, more fundamental question: (a) Did a powerful man, Mr Liew Mun Leong, and I will refer to him as LML, work the system to his advantage?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: (b) Did the Police and AGC unfairly prosecute Ms Liyani, because LML was the complainant?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: (c) Did Ms Liyani get a fair trial in the State Courts?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: (d) Do we have one law for the wealthy, socially connected, and another for the rest of society?

sections.label: Rule of Law and equality
sections.summary: The credibility of the system and foundation of society depends on ensuring Rule of Law and that the Law applies equally to all.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The credibility of our system, the foundation of our society depends on us ensuring that there is Rule of Law and the Law applies equally to all.

sections.label: Ms Liyani's employment history
sections.summary: Ms Liyani was an Indonesian domestic worker in Singapore since 1997; MOM records show LML was her seventh employer, and she worked for him from March 2007 until 28 October 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Liyani was an Indonesian domestic worker working in Singapore since 1997.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: According to her, LML was her third employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But MOM records show that LML was in fact her seventh employer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: She worked for LML from March 2007 until 28 October 2016.

sections.label: Karl Liew dismisses Ms Liyani
sections.summary: On 28 October 2016, Karl Liew went to LML's residence with employment agents at LML's request, told her there were missing items, and she was asked to pack her belongings and given compensation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 28 October 2016, at about 11 am, Karl Liew – I will refer to him as Karl – LML's son, went to LML’s residence at 49 CL with employment agents and this was at LML’s request.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Karl told her that “there are missing items in the house and the only people staying in the house were my father, my mother and you”.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: She was asked to pack her belongings and given two months’ salary as compensation, in addition to that month’s salary.

sections.label: LML lodges Police report
sections.summary: On 30 October 2016 at 3.54 pm, LML lodged a Police report at Tanglin Police Station.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 30 October 2016 at 3.54 pm, LML lodged a Police report at Tanglin Police Station.

sections.label: Police file sent to AGC
sections.summary: On 5 June 2017 the Police sent the file to AGC with investigation findings and recommendations; AGC handles about 3,000 theft reports yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 5 June 2017, the Police sent the file to AGC with their investigation findings and recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Over the last three years, AGC has dealt with an average about 3,000 reports every year for theft in dwelling and theft as servant offences.

sections.label: AGC decision to charge Liyani
sections.summary: AGC charged Ms Liyani because there was sufficient evidence theft offences were likely committed and prosecution was in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: AGC decided to charge Ms Liyani for two main reasons: there was sufficient evidence which showed that theft offences were likely to have been committed; and second, it was in the public interest to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The evidence before AGC at that time was as follows: the Liews had identified all the items in the charges as items belonging to them and gave some detail.

sections.label: Liyani admission to taking clothing
sections.summary: Ms Liyani expressly admitted to taking some items, namely 10 to 15 items of clothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Liyani also expressly admitted to taking some items – 10 to 15 items of clothing.

sections.label: Liyani second statement on clothing
sections.summary: In her second statement dated 4 December 2016, Ms Liyani said she only took about 10 to 15 pieces of men's clothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In her second statement dated 4 December 2016, Ms Liyani said, "I only took about 10 to 15 pieces of men's clothing belonging to my employer's husband.

sections.label: AGC view on prosecuting Liyani
sections.summary: AGC viewed there was a case to prosecute and a clear public interest in prosecuting Ms Liyani.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Putting together Ms Liyani's apparent inconsistencies, her answers on the jewellery and the other items, which she said she found in the trash – like the Prada bag, the two Apple iPhones, a pair of Gucci sunglasses – her other questionable answers, her admission to taking some male clothing without permission, AGC's view was that there was a case to prosecute.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: AGC also took the view that there was a clear public interest in prosecuting Ms Liyani.

sections.label: State Courts trial duration
sections.summary: The trial was heard in the State Courts over 20 days, from 23 April 2018 to 17 January 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The trial was heard in the State Courts over 20 days, from 23 April 2018 to 17 January 2019.

sections.label: High Court acquits Liyani
sections.summary: The High Court acquitted Ms Liyani on all charges, finding reasonable doubt about the Liews' motive for making allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On appeal, the High Court acquitted Ms Liyani on all charges.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court's decision was premised on two key findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, there was reasonable doubt as to whether the Liews had an improper motive for making allegations against Ms Liyani.

sections.label: High Court motive finding
sections.summary: The High Court found reasonable doubt about whether the Liews filed the Police Report to prevent Ms Liyani filing a MOM complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In this case, the High Court came to a view on motive that there was reasonable doubt as to whether the Liews filed the Police Report, to prevent Ms Liyani from filing a MOM complaint against them for having deployed her to work outside their house.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Motive appears to have been a key factor in the Judgment and we have looked carefully at what the High Court said at paragraph 52 of the Judgment, that Ms Liyani had made explicit to two members of LML’s family her intention to lodge a complaint to MOM about being required to work illegally at Karl’s residence at 39 CL and at Karl’s office.

sections.label: High Court inference on complaint
sections.summary: The High Court inferred Ms Liyani said she would complain about working outside LML's house, giving reasonable doubt on motive.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court did note this and said that Ms Liyani did not actually say that she was going to complain about having been made to work at Karl’s house or office.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, when the High Court said Ms Liyani had made explicit to two members of the Liew family she was going to complain about having been made to work outside LML’s house, the statement was an inference that the High Court has made based on the evidence and submissions before it.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Based on this, the High Court also said LML and Karl must have been concerned and, therefore, there is reasonable doubt as to whether they had a motive to make allegations and a police report against Ms Liyani.

sections.label: Liyani complaint about short notice
sections.summary: The subsequent evidence is that she said she wanted to complain because she was given too short notice.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The subsequent evidence is that she said, and I quote, "I want to complain because you gave me too short notice".

sections.label: Liyani dismissed 28 October 2016
sections.summary: Ms Liyani was dismissed on 28 October 2016 because a new helper had become available that day.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Liyani was dismissed on 28 October 2016 because a new helper had become available on that day.

sections.label: Family decides Liyani dismissal date
sections.summary: On 26 October 2016, after checking with the maid agent, the family decided Ms Liyani would be dismissed on 28 October 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On 26 October 2016, after checking with the maid agent on the status of the new helper, the family decided that Ms Liyani would be dismissed on 28 October 2016.

sections.label: Maid agents offered complaint help
sections.summary: On 28 October 2016 maid agents twice offered to help Ms Liyani lodge an MOM complaint, but she declined.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Further investigations also revealed that on 28 October 2016, the maid agents offered twice to assist Ms Liyani with lodging an MOM complaint but Ms Liyani declined.

sections.label: Liyani complaint after being charged
sections.summary: Ms Liyani lodged her illegal deployment complaint after being charged in September and October 2017, and the Prosecution did not put forward this evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Liyani lodged her complaint about illegal deployment after she was charged in September and October 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As can be seen from Annex 5, the Prosecution did not obtain or put forward this evidence because the issue had not been raised by the Defence in its Case for Defence or at the pre-trial conference.

sections.label: Police report and MOM complaint
sections.summary: A Police Report would not prevent Ms Liyani from returning to Singapore or from filing an MOM complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Making a Police Report will not prevent Ms Liyani from returning to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Indeed, in this case, it did not stop her from returning to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And making a Police Report will also not prevent Ms Liyani from filing a complaint with MOM if she was serious about doing so.

sections.label: Police and AGC theft case basis
sections.summary: The passage asks whether, on the material before them, the Police and AGC had good reason to treat this as a routine theft case.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On the material before them, did the Police and AGC have good reason to proceed on the basis that this was a routine theft case?

sections.label: Liyani employment termination not sudden
sections.summary: Investigations showed the decision to terminate Ms Liyani's employment was not sudden; she was terminated on 28 October 2016 when the replacement helper became available.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The investigations showed that the decision to terminate Ms Liyani's employment was not sudden.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Liews decided upon a replacement helper in September 2016 for the reasons set out earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Ms Liyani's employment was terminated on 28 October 2016 because the replacement helper became available then.

sections.label: High Court chain of custody break
sections.summary: The High Court said there was a break in the chain of custody of the items alleged to have been stolen by Ms Liyani.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court said that there was a break in the chain of custody of the items which were alleged to have been stolen by Ms Liyani.

sections.label: Items Liyani denies packing
sections.summary: The only question is ownership of items she admits packing, while she denies packing two DVD players, clothing, bedsheets and a blanket.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Where she admits to packing the items, or taking the items, then the only question is whether it belongs to the Liews or to Ms Liyani, or for some reason, she is entitled to keep the items.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have identified the items which Ms Liyani does not admit to packing into her boxes, namely the two DVD players, some of the clothing said to belong to Karl, three bedsheets and one blanket said to belong to Karl.

sections.label: Break in chain of custody
sections.summary: Removing items affected by the break in chain of custody still leaves four theft charges, and the Police admitted a lapse.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we remove those items possibly affected by the break in chain of custody, there would still be four theft charges against Ms Liyani.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As regards the items that were affected by the break in the chain, there is no question – the Police should have acted faster.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police admitted that there was a lapse in this area of investigation and I will come back to this later.

sections.label: AGC policy on perjury findings
sections.summary: AGC will consider further investigations and proceedings when judgments contain findings of perjury or other serious offences, and Karl was investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Arising from this case – and this is an important statement of policy – AGC has decided that hereafter, if any judgment or decision issued in the course of any legal proceedings, contains findings that there may have been perjury or other serious offences, AGC will seriously consider whether there should be further investigations, proceedings, in respect of those indicated offences.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Karl has been investigated as to whether he committed any criminal offences, including perjury.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A statement will be announced later this evening based on these investigations.

sections.label: Expert on watch values
sections.summary: An expert witness said the Helix watch was of no value and the Vacheron Constantin and Swatch watches were counterfeit and valueless.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: An expert witness said that the Helix watch was of "no value", and the Vacheron Constantin and Swatch watches were counterfeit and had no value.

sections.label: Police and AGC assessment
sections.summary: The Police and AGC thought she was untruthful, assessed that she did steal, and charged her.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police and AGC thought she was untruthful.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They assessed that she did steal and that is why she was charged.

sections.label: Courts on her truthfulness
sections.summary: The State Court found her quite untruthful, while the High Court gave her the benefit of doubt due to Karl's statements and other inconsistencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The State Court found her to be quite untruthful.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court gave her the benefit of doubt because it was troubled by Karl's improbable, unreliable statements; some other inconsistencies in the Liews' testimonies and their conduct.

sections.label: CPC breach, no interpreter
sections.summary: The High Court found section 22(4) of the CPC breached because Ms Liyani lacked a Bahasa Indonesia interpreter for her first four statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court found that there had been a breach of section 22(4) of the CPC, because Ms Liyani had not been given a Bahasa Indonesia interpreter for her first four statements.

sections.label: Theft case, foreign domestic workers
sections.summary: A prima facie theft case was disclosed, with about 250,000 foreign domestic workers in Singapore employed by over 200,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: They disclosed a prima facie case of theft.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There are about 250,000 foreign domestic workers in Singapore, employed by more than 200,000 families.

sections.label: Police criminal cases 2016
sections.summary: Police investigated about 66,200 criminal cases in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Police investigated about 66,200 criminal cases in 2016.

sections.label: Theft arrests and prosecutions
sections.summary: Of 66,200 cases, 14,122 were theft-related; 500 were arrested under section 381, 246 foreign domestic workers, 58 prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of the 66,200 cases, 14,122 were theft-related offences, in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we drill down to theft as a servant, under section 381 of the Penal Code, there were 500 arrests in 2016 of whom 246 were foreign domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Of those 246 arrests, 58 were prosecuted – 24%.

sections.label: Gap in police review
sections.summary: There was a gap between the Police report filed on 30 October 2016 and the Police looking at the items on 3 December 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, that there was a gap between the Police report being filed on 30 October 2016 and the Police looking at the items, on 3 December 2016.

sections.label: Internal investigations into officers
sections.summary: Internal investigations are being carried out on the conduct of officers involved in this case and action will be taken as necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Nevertheless, internal investigations are being carried out in relation to the conduct of the officers involved in this case and action will be taken, as necessary.

sections.label: Police workload and manpower
sections.summary: Workload review for Police investigation officers is tied to manpower issues, with online case management systems being explored.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a general situation in some workplaces, many workplaces in Singapore with tight manpower issues, particularly in several areas of the Civil Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have asked for a review of the workload of Police investigation officers, though quite frankly, there is no easy solution because fundamentally, it is a manpower issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police are also looking into online case management systems, to prompt officers on next steps in investigative workflows and ensure accountability and minimise the risk of lapses in investigations.

sections.label: Liyani photos and interpreter
sections.summary: Colour photos were shown to Ms Liyani in her final statement with a Bahasa Indonesia interpreter provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Colour photos were shown to Ms Liyani in her final statement when a Bahasa Indonesia interpreter was also provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Police will take on board the High Court's comments, which are fair.

sections.label: Timing of taking statements
sections.summary: The Police accept the point made about the time when statements are taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police accept the point made about the time when statements are taken.

sections.label: Appeals against conviction 2018-2019
sections.summary: In 2018 and 2019, 16 appeals against conviction were reversed, nine from State Courts and seven from High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2018 and 2019, there were 16 appeals by the accused against conviction, when the Appellate Court disagreed with the Lower Court and reversed the decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Nine were appeals from the State Courts to the High Court and seven were appeals from the High Court to the Court of Appeal.

sections.label: PP v GCK conviction reversal
sections.summary: In PP v GCK, the Court of Appeal reinstated a molest conviction and substituted a 16-month sentence with three strokes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In another case, PP v GCK   SGCA 2, the State Court convicted the accused for outrage of modesty.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He was sentenced to 22 months’ imprisonment, three strokes of the cane.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The High Court reversed the conviction, and acquitted the accused, on the basis that there was insufficient evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: On a criminal reference, the Court of Appeal reinstated the conviction but substituted the original sentence, with a sentence of 16 months’ imprisonment and three strokes of the cane.

sections.label: Theft case handled normally
sections.summary: The case was treated as any other theft case, with no pressure or influence from LML or anyone acting for him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have said it earlier and I will reiterate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It was treated as any other theft case and handled accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have checked with the IOs, their supervisor, the DPPs and their director.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There was no pressure or influence exerted on them by LML or anyone acting on his behalf, and they handled this case as they have handled other theft cases.

sections.label: Case not known to senior management
sections.summary: The case did not come to the attention of senior management at the Police or the Ministry.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The case did not come to the attention of the senior management either at the Police or in my Ministry.

sections.label: No lobbying or pressure
sections.summary: No one lobbied or exerted pressure on the investigation officers, the supervisor, or anyone able to influence the investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: No one lobbied or exerted pressure either on the IOs or on the supervisor, or on anyone in a position to influence the investigations.

sections.label: AG unaware until trial
sections.summary: AG did not know of the investigations or proceedings until the case went for trial.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: AG did not know of these investigations or proceedings until the case went for trial.

sections.label: AG fairness perception review
sections.summary: AG felt the perception of fairness may be affected if he oversaw the review, given his history of differences with LML.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: AG felt that given the history of differences he has had with LML, the perception of fairness may be affected if AG oversaw the review.

sections.label: Teh Cheang Wan example
sections.summary: The case of Mr Teh Cheang Wan is a prime example of the approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The case of Mr Teh Cheang Wan is a prime example of the approach.

sections.label: Teh leave and death
sections.summary: Mr Teh was placed on leave of absence and chose to end his life rather than face trial or corruption charges the AGC had yet to settle.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Teh was placed on leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: He ultimately chose to end his life rather than face trial or corruption charges, which the AGC had then yet to settle.

sections.label: Corruption cases of public officials
sections.summary: Three officials were convicted: Peter Lim for corruption, Edwin Yeo for misappropriating money, and TT Durai for corruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2012, you had Peter Lim, Commissioner of SCDF – in fact, he was Commissioner of SCDF when I was Minister for Home Affairs too – convicted of corruption charges for receiving sexual favours with three different women, sentenced to six months' imprisonment, dismissed from public service following disciplinary proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2013, you had Mr Edwin Yeo, Assistant Director of CPIB, misappropriating money, jailed for 10 years for criminal breach of trust or CBT as a public servant and forgery.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2007, you had Mr TT Durai, CEO of the National Kidney Foundation, convicted for corruption, sentenced to imprisonment; appeal to the High Court dismissed.

sections.label: Action against wrongdoing
sections.summary: The message is that action will be taken against anyone who does wrong, regardless of who they are.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The message is it does not matter who you are, if you do wrong, action will be taken.

sections.label: MPs must uphold clean standards
sections.summary: MPs must uphold rigorous standards, never compromise them, and never give cause for allegations of misusing their position or access to Ministers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The reputation for clean, incorruptible government is one of our most precious assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I cannot stress strongly enough every Member of Parliament (MP) must uphold the rigorous standards we have set for ourselves, do nothing to compromise them, never give cause for allegations that you are misusing your position, especially your access to Ministers.

sections.label: No exploiting public position
sections.summary: Government MPs must not exploit their public position, contacts with Ministers, or access to departments and civil servants for personal interest or employers' benefit.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: You must not exploit your public position as Government MPs, your close contacts with the Ministers, or your access to government departments and civil servants, for your personal interest or the benefit of your employers.

sections.label: Unresolved issues end MP status
sections.summary: When they leave, the issue is usually resolved, and if it is not resolved, they do not remain as MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: When they leave, the issue is usually resolved.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And if it is not resolved, then they do not remain as MPs.

sections.label: Attorney-General recused from review
sections.summary: The Attorney-General recused himself from the review because of his history with LML.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Earlier I had said, the Attorney-General recused himself from the review because of his history with LML.

sections.label: Lobbying and enforcement
sections.summary: Big Pharma spent US$4.45 billion on lobbying over 22 years, and one study found regulators 45% less likely to enforce against lobbying banks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Big Pharma, for example, spent US$4.45 billion on lobbying alone over the last 22 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One study found that regulators were 45% less likely to initiate enforcement action against banks that lobby versus banks that do not.

sections.label: Clean system and leadership
sections.summary: Singapore avoided influence peddling because its three Prime Ministers had the will and decisiveness to keep a clean system.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But these factors are also present in many countries where influence peddling is, nevertheless, a cancer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have avoided that slippery path because, in addition to the above, we have had in our three Prime Ministers the strong will to ensure a clean system and the decisiveness to act when something goes wrong.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And always, always, regardless of your rules and regardless of your systems, the rot starts at the top.

sections.label: Theft as Servant arrests
sections.summary: Theft as a Servant averages 528 arrests annually, about 48% of them foreign domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: For the specific offence of Theft as a Servant, an average of 528 arrests annually, about 48% of them are foreign domestic workers.

sections.label: Employers prosecuted for offences
sections.summary: From 2015 to 2019, 115 employers were prosecuted for offences against foreign domestic workers; 65 convicted, 21 pending.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: At the same time, on the reverse side of the coin, from 2015 to 2019, 115 employers were prosecuted for committing offences against foreign domestic workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Sixty-five persons have been convicted, 21 cases are pending.

sections.label: Police-to-population ratios
sections.summary: Police officer ratios to population are New York 0.42%, London 0.34%, Hong Kong 0.39%, Singapore 0.23% including full-time National Servicemen.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Just to give Members a sense, the ratio of Police officers to population – I have spoken about this previously in the House and I am here referring to Police officers in general, not just IOs – New York at 0.42%, London at 0.34%, Hong Kong at 0.39%, Singapore at 0.23%, including full-time National Servicemen.

sections.label: Legal Service specialisation tracks
sections.summary: In 2014 the Prime Minister announced greater Legal Service specialisation, creating separate Legal and Judicial career tracks for middle-rank LSOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In 2014, the Prime Minister announced greater specialisation in the Legal Service.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: There are now two separate career tracks for the middle ranks of LSOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One is the “Legal” track and the other is the “Judicial” track.

sections.label: Legal and Judicial career tracks
sections.summary: The Legal Service Commission introduced two separate career tracks for LSOs up to Grade 3, the Legal and Judicial tracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Hence, we need more specialist and expert skills than ever before.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Thus, the Legal Service Commission or LSC introduced two separate career tracks for LSOs up to Grade 3 – the "Legal" and "Judicial" tracks.

sections.label: Two new Personnel Boards
sections.summary: Two new Personnel Boards under the LSC were established to oversee the Legal and Judicial career tracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: To oversee the two career tracks, two new Personnel Boards under the LSC – the Legal Branch Personnel Board and the Judicial Branch Personnel Board – were established.

sections.label: Median time for criminal cases
sections.summary: The median time for a criminal case from first charge in Court to judgment is 15 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: First, on the trial processes, the median time taken in the Courts for a criminal case from being first charged in Court to judgment is 15 months – median.

sections.label: Foreigners in criminal cases
sections.summary: 22% of cases involved foreigners, and a 51-year-old Singaporean charged with shop theft was convicted and jailed 16 weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: About a quarter, 22% of these cases, involved foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, having a criminal case pending, why should we make Singaporeans suffer disproportionately more?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We had a 51-year old Singaporean accused person charged in March of this year for two counts of shop theft.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In June 2020, AGC assessed that his remand period, three months at that point, might outstrip his possible sentence even if he were to be convicted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: A two-day trial was conducted, after which he was convicted and sentenced to 16 weeks' of jail.

sections.label: Government share of CLAS costs
sections.summary: The Government pays 75% of CLAS' operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government pays 75% of CLAS' operating costs.

sections.label: Money for honoraria
sections.summary: Where accused are Singapore Citizens or PRs, the money can also be used to pay honoraria.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Where the accused are Singapore Citizens or PRs, the money can also be used to pay honoraria.

sections.label: Virendra Rastogi criminal legal aid
sections.summary: Virendra Rastogi, a London metals trading tycoon, owned a S$10.55-million home, arrived in a chauffeur-driven car and received S$8.79 million in criminal legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One of these was Virendra Rastogi, a London metals trading tycoon, who owned a S$10.55-million home, arrived in court every day in a chauffeur-driven car and he received S$8.79 million worth of criminal legal aid.

sections.label: Drug dealer legal aid delays
sections.summary: A convicted drug dealer kept his alleged $7.9 million fortune due to delays in finding a legal aid lawyer, and lawyers won a $40 million fee rise after the 2018 strike.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In one case, a convicted drug dealer was allowed to keep his alleged $7.9 million fortune because of delays in finding a legal aid lawyer to represent him in confiscation hearings.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The lawyers' protests eventually resulted in more watered down reforms, continued escalating legal aid costs for the government and legal aid lawyers won a $40 million fee rise after the 2018 strike.

sections.label: Hong Kong legal aid spending
sections.summary: Hong Kong spent $217 million on civil and criminal legal aid in 2017, with budgets escalating due to lawyers' fees rising around 4% to 10% yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Hong Kong spent a total of $217 million on both civil and criminal legal aid in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Hong Kong has also experienced escalating legal aid budgets due to continued increase in lawyers' fees of around 4% to 10% every year.

sections.label: CLAS income coverage
sections.summary: CLAS today covers the lowest 25% in terms of household income.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: CLAS today covers the lowest 25% in terms of household income.

sections.label: Public defender's office option
sections.summary: The public defender's office, together with the means and merits test, seems like a good option.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In this context, the public defender's office, assisting together with the means and merits test, seems like a good option.

sections.label: Government considering public defender's office
sections.summary: The Government is considering a public defender's office, preferring it in principle, and will study its details and feasibility with the Law Society and criminal bar.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The primary factor will be, as I have said, to ensure that those who cannot afford lawyers can get access to justice without the situation becoming fiscally difficult for the taxpayer and the Government is discussing but in principle prefers the approach of a public defender's office.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, the answer to Ms Carrie Tan's question is yes.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have been and we are considering seriously a public defender's office.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We will study the details and feasibility of this further in consultation with the Law Society and the criminal bar.

sections.label: Committee of Inquiry over AGC
sections.summary: The speaker says he cannot appoint a Committee of Inquiry into the AGC because it does not report to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I assume his concern is whether there was any undue influence by or on behalf of the Liews on the Police or AGC in this matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it will be clear to Mr Leong if he had looked at section 9 that I do not have the power to appoint a Committee of Inquiry in respect of AGC because it is not an agency that reports to me.

sections.label: Commission of Inquiry recommendation conditions
sections.summary: The speaker will recommend a Commission of Inquiry if the Member states its scope and confirms he will attend, and officers confirmed no improper pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: That is very high level, headed by a Supreme Court judge or someone qualified to be a Supreme Court judge.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am prepared to recommend to the Cabinet that we have a Commission of Inquiry but the Member should first tell us what he wants this Commission of Inquiry to look into and he should confirm that he will come to the Commission of Inquiry and state his position.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The officers involved, both AGC and the Police, have confirmed categorically no improper pressure.

sections.label: Difference between inquiry types
sections.summary: The speaker notes the difference between a Committee of Inquiry and a Commission of Inquiry and asks if an independent inquiry is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To answer the Minister, first of all, I am aware there is a difference between a Committee of Inquiry and a Commission of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Do we all agree that there is a need to have an independent inquiry into this case?

sections.label: Influence peddling and inquiry powers
sections.summary: The speaker says influence peddling is involved and questions why he was asked to do something not possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is not just influence peddling that we are talking about here.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I do not understand why if you knew the difference between a Committee of Inquiry and a Commission of Inquiry, you have asked me to do something that is not possible.

sections.label: Scope of proposed Commission of Inquiry
sections.summary: The speaker asks what exactly is being sought and says he will recommend a Commission of Inquiry to the Cabinet.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, what is it exactly that you are looking for?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I will be prepared to recommend to the Cabinet to hold a Commission of Inquiry.

sections.label: Five weeks delay no excuse
sections.summary: The speaker tells Mr Leong that there is no excuse for the five weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Leong, if it is the five weeks, I have told you, I said to the House, there is no excuse for the five weeks.

sections.label: Five weeks inquiry refusal
sections.summary: The speaker is not prepared to recommend a Commission of Inquiry about the five weeks because the question does not make sense to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If it is about the five weeks, I am not prepared to recommend a Commission of Inquiry for that purpose, because the question you asked does not make sense to me.

sections.label: Foreign domestic workers and families
sections.summary: The speaker cites 250,000 foreign domestic workers and about 200,000 families, and says a Government Commission of Inquiry must look at Government institutions and organs.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Mr Leong, I have said that there are 250,000 foreign domestic workers and about 200,000 families.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government Commission of Inquiry has got to look at Government institutions and organs.

sections.label: AGC and Police evidence
sections.summary: The speaker explained the prima facie evidence AGC and Police had, and says a Commission of Inquiry cannot legally look into employers' and maids' conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I explained what was the evidence that AGC and the Police had, so that Members understood what was the prima facie evidence that Police and AGC had.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is legally not possible to hold a Commission of Inquiry to look into the conduct of employers and maids.

sections.label: High Court comments and next steps
sections.summary: The speaker says facts emerged from investigations after High Court comments, an announcement on next steps will be made, and he will not recommend an inquiry into motive.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have also said as a result of the High Court's comments, the investigations, some facts came out which we are disclosing to you.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have also said later this evening an announcement will be made as to what are the next steps to be taken as a result of those investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I am not prepared to recommend a Commission of Inquiry to look into this issue of motive.

sections.label: Specific matter inquiry offer
sections.summary: The speaker says if there is something specific, it should be put down and a Commission of Inquiry will be held.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If there is something specific, put it down, we will hold a Commission of Inquiry.

sections.label: Breach of Police rules
sections.summary: The speaker says distribution during the break was supposed to happen, a breach of Police rules and law is being disciplined, and he will check the rules and share details with Mr Singh.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: During the break, they were supposed to have distributed but we will try and make sure of that.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a breach of Police rules, it is a breach of the law and disciplinary action is being taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I will have to check whether the rules allow this but if the rules allow this, I will find out the details of what happened and I am happy to share it with Mr Singh, when eventually it is dealt with.

sections.label: Review of IO pressure
sections.summary: The Minister says he asked how often IOs are under such pressure and a review will report back to him.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And in my Ministerial Statement I said I have asked myself how often are IOs under such kind of pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, there is a review, the Police will come back to me and let me know how much pressure they are under.

sections.label: Extent of IO pressure
sections.summary: The Minister says the issue is common to both sides and he has asked about the extent of the pressure.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is common to both sides of the House on this issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I have asked on the extent of the pressure and I will get a better sense of it.

sections.label: Ms Liyani and Police response
sections.summary: The Minister says Ms Liyani is not doing this and the Police will deal with it and respond in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And I think, Mr Singh, we all know that Ms Liyani is not doing this.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But the Police will deal with it and will respond in due course.

sections.label: Liews' police report motive
sections.summary: A Member quotes Justice Chan Seng Onn on improper motive by Mr Liew and Mr Karl and asks about further investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I took out a copy of the judgment issued by Justice Chan Seng Onn and in one of his statements, he had said that, "I find the Prosecution had failed to dispel the reasonable doubt raised by the Defence and showed that there was no improper motive by Mr Liew and Mr Karl in making the Police report." I was wondering if the Minister clarify whether the Liews have an improper motive in filing this Police report.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Also, the further investigation that was necessitated by the High Court's comments.

sections.label: Case duration and AGC papers
sections.summary: The Minister says papers took about six months to mid-2017 to reach AGC, with back and forth after.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The duration of the case, and I will have to stand corrected if I get anything wrong here.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think it took about six months to June, middle of 2017, for the papers to be sent to AGC and then there was back and forth as I had said between AGC and the Police.

sections.label: Foreign domestic worker theft prosecutions
sections.summary: The Minister states that for foreign domestic workers, 25% of theft cases go for prosecution.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As you notice, if you take foreign domestic workers, 25% of the theft cases go for prosecution.

sections.label: Number of appeal judges
sections.summary: The question is whether to return to two and five judges on appeal, which needs discussion and the Government is not implicitly opposed to.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Member's question is whether we go back to two judges and five judges on appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is not something that implicitly the Government is opposed to, but it is something that will need to be discussed.

sections.label: Statement-taking and phased rollout
sections.summary: With that, there can be no questions about statement-taking; phases were announced, Phase 1 done and Phase 2 earlier this year, but a serious bottleneck exists.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Once you have that, there can be no questions about what happened during the statement-taking.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have announced it in phases: Phase 1 has taken place, Phase 2 was earlier this year, but there is a serious bottleneck.

sections.label: Automatic transcription not mature
sections.summary: Automatic transcription technology is not yet mature enough for the document to be precise and used in court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Because today, the technology for automatic transcription is not yet mature enough for the document to be precise, to be used in court.

sections.label: Video recording and expansion delay
sections.summary: That held back expansion, and the first video recording case is going to or is in Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, that is what held us back from expanding.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think the first case where video recording has been done, is going to Court or is in Court.

sections.label: Arrest release and counsel access
sections.summary: A 2019 Police study found 96% of arrested persons are released within 48 hours and can consult counsel; longer remand requires a Court application, and since March 2006 an Access to Counsel Scheme applies.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The current situation is that 96% of the persons arrested – this is based on a 2019 study by Police – are released within 48 hours of the arrest.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Immediately after they are released, 48 hours, they are able to consult legal counsel.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Where it is necessary to continue remanding a person for longer than 48 hours, the Police will have to apply to Court; and the Court will, of course, weigh the different considerations in deciding to order further remand.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Since March 2006, the Police have had an Access to Counsel Scheme to grant an accused person access to counsel during this remand period, as long as investigations have been completed or are nearing completion.

sections.label: Accounting of steps taken
sections.summary: An accounting of steps taken shows prima facie a good case to proceed, with confirmations on how the matter was dealt with and no influence-peddling or influence exerted.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And an accounting of the steps they have taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And that shows prima facie that there was a good case to proceed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And the confirmations that have been given here about how the matter was dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And that there was no influence-peddling or influence exerted.

sections.label: Police investigation lapses and High Court
sections.summary: Speaker questions the Police's five-week lapse, failure to seize evidence, and differing reasons given by the officer, and explains further investigations arose from the High Court's decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The sense I am getting is that he is saying that if the High Court had known certain other information at the time, the High Court might have come to different conclusions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The second clarification is regarding the lapses in the Police investigation which he spoke about earlier.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He mentioned that the five-week lapse from the time that the case was reported, to the time that the Police actually attended the scene and also the failure to seize the evidence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He said that there was some internal review done and the officer had said that he was very busy at the time and also he had some personal matter to attend to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, I believe that during the trial, he actually gave a different reason and his reason was that he did not want to re-victimise the Liew family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Speaking as a former Police officer, I find this is quite unusual in a theft case that an officer would consider this issue of re-victimisation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And of course, I accept the fact that LML did not exert pressure on the officers, but I am just wondering whether it crossed the Minister's mind that the officer himself may have felt that he was dealing with somebody who was very prominent and therefore he needed to take extra care.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I explained that we did not go about looking for any further evidence to question the High Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It was the High Court's decision which required us to do further investigations specifically on the Liews and whether any criminal investigations had been committed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, in the course of the investigations, we came across further evidence.

sections.label: Five-week lapse a breach
sections.summary: The speaker emphasises that the five-week lapse is a breach and will be dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The five weeks – first of all, I want to emphasise over and over again.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is a breach and it will be dealt with.

sections.label: Police approach to seizing evidence
sections.summary: The speaker says Police now try not to seize items if identification is good, but the officer's photographs were inadequate in quality and method.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: By the time it was released, it had gone down quite substantially.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think the Police approach, generally now, is to try not to seize, as far as possible, if you can get good identification of the items.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Police officer assessed that photographs were enough.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But having assessed that, the quality of the photographs was not adequate and the way the photographs was taken was not adequate.

sections.label: Legal Service Commission and judicial commission
sections.summary: The Minister responds to a suggestion of a separate Judicial Service Commission, citing case numbers, available prosecutors and investigators, and calling the current integrated model best for now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, in relation to the fact that currently, we have a Legal Service Commission, which draws on both judicial officers as well as legal officers from the AGC, I wonder whether the Minister has any views on having a separate Judicial Service Commission.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think the first point made by Mr Murali Pillai about having AGC, greater degree of legal expertise coming up at an early stage is a good one.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I have given you some numbers just now, the thousands of cases that are handled.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think given the number, if you look at the Public Prosecutors we have available, if you look at the IOs we have available, to do that in an integrated way from the beginning, I think would be very challenging.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I know Mr Murali Pillai says for a case that is complex.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think we will have to look at these possibilities and identify which case is complex; and sometimes, cases start out as simple and end up as complex.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Again, the answer is what I have given earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I have given a fairly long answer on how our service is structured, and where it is integrated and where it is separate.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I think given the size and given the inherent limitations, that is probably the best model for the time being.
